text: This thesis presents a comprehensive study on the design and implementation of a multi-objective adaptive Linear Quadratic Regulator (LQR) controller with battery aging compensation for urban micro-electric vehicle (micro-EV) powertrain systems. The pro-posed controller addresses critical challenges in electric vehicle control, including energy efficiency optimization, battery state-of-health (SoH) degradation, and multi-objective trade-offs between performance metrics.

chapter: ABSTRACT
text: The research introduces two main contributions: (1) an adaptive LQR framework that dynamically adjusts controller gains based on real-time battery state-of-health esti-mation, and (2) a Pareto optimization approach for balancing energy consumption and battery longevity using the NSGA-II algorithm. The battery aging model incorporates SEI (Solid Electrolyte Interphase) layer growth following the Arrhenius law, while the SoH estimator employs Coulomb counting with adaptive correction based on voltage feedback.

CHAPTER 1: INTRODUCTION
text: The global automotive industry is undergoing a fundamental transformation from in-ternal combustion engine (ICE) vehicles to electric vehicles (EVs), driven by mounting environmental concerns, stringent emission regulations, and declining battery costs. Ac-cording to the International Energy Agency (IEA) Global EV Outlook 2024 [1], global EV sales reached 14 million units in 2023, representing a 35% year-over-year increase, with projections indicating that EVs will account for over 40% of new vehicle sales by 2030. This transition is particularly pronounced in Southeast Asia, where governments are implementing aggressive policies to accelerate EV adoption and reduce transportation-related emissions.

chapter: CHAPTER 1: INTRODUCTION
text: Vietnam has emerged as a significant player in the EV market, led by VinFast’s am-bitious electrification strategy and the entry of international micro-EV manufacturers such as Wuling Motors. The micro-EV segment, defined by the United Nations Regula-tions L6e and L7e as light quadricycles with maximum speeds below 45 km/h and power outputs below 4 kW (L6e) or 15 kW (L7e), represents a compelling solution for urban mobility in Vietnamese cities. These vehicles offer affordable entry points for electric mobility, with compact dimensions suitable for dense urban environments and reduced infrastructure requirements compared to conventional EVs.

chapter: CHAPTER 1: INTRODUCTION
text: The electrification of urban transportation in Vietnam addresses several critical chal-lenges. First, air pollution in major cities has reached alarming levels, with Hanoi and Ho Chi Minh City consistently ranking among the most polluted cities globally accord-ing to the WHO Ambient Air Pollution database [2]. Second, Vietnam’s dependence on imported petroleum products for transportation creates significant economic vulnerabili-ties and balance-of-payments pressures. Third, the urban mobility patterns in Vietnamese cities, characterized by short trip distances, high stop-and-go frequency, and constrained parking, align well with the capabilities and limitations of micro-EVs.

subsection: Contribution 2: Multi-Objective Pareto Optimization for Energy-Battery-Longevity Trade-offs
last_caption: Figure 1. Research Methodology Framework
text: The thesis presents a comprehensive framework for Pareto-optimal design of EV powertrain controllers that explicitly considers the trade-off between energy ef-ficiency, driving performance, and battery longevity. Using the Non-dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm II (NSGA-II), the framework generates a detailed Pareto front enabling designers to select operating points based on specific application re-quirements.

chapter: CHAPTER 1: INTRODUCTION
subsection: Contribution 2: Multi-Objective Pareto Optimization for Energy-Battery-Longevity Trade-offs
last_caption: Figure 1. Research Methodology Framework
text: The optimization formulation minimizes two objective functions: energy consump-tion per kilometer and battery capacity fade rate. The objectives are subject to stability constraints (positive definite solution to the algebraic Riccati equation), tracking accuracy constraints (steady-state error less than 2% of reference), and physical constraints on controller gains. The resulting Pareto front reveals the fun-damental trade-offs inherent in EV powertrain control and provides quantitative guidance for controller design.

text: Figure 10 illustrates the complete system architecture. The Vietnam Urban Cycle (VUC) generates the velocity reference profile, which is compared with the measured vehicle velocity to produce the tracking error signal. The adaptive LQR controller pro-cesses the error and generates motor torque commands. The motor drive converts torque commands to inverter switching signals. The vehicle dynamics block models the vehicle response to motor torque. The Extended Kalman Filter-based SoH estimator continu-ously monitors battery condition and provides the adaptive gain to the LQR controller.
